note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Cough for several days with runny nose; cough described as continuous and dry, kept patient awake at night; throat irritated from coughing.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms started about 5–6 days ago; ongoing.
- Associated symptoms: Fatigue/lethargy; chills; muscle aches; brief episode of diarrhea at onset (resolved); no nausea or vomiting; no chest pain; no shortness of breath at rest; no fever measured.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin; lisinopril.
- Allergies: None.
- Social history: Lives with partner; former smoker (quit ~6 months ago); consumes wine (2–3 glasses, 3 evenings per week); advised reducing alcohol. Works as IT developer.
- Family history: Father with type 2 diabetes.

Objective:
- No vital signs or full physical examination findings documented.
- ENT: patient reports ears are fine; no pain or discharge.
- Respiratory: patient reports dry cough; no productive sputum; no clear evidence of laboured breathing on interview.
- Other: patient reports fatigue and generalized muscle soreness; no abdominal symptoms currently.
- Additional notes: Temperature not measured; no objective fever documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Viral upper respiratory infection with dry cough
- Assessment: Viral illness (likely viral URI) with dry cough and fatigue.
- Differential diagnoses (if applicable): Common cold; influenza; bronchitis; other viral URIs.
- Investigations planned: None at this time; return if symptoms persist or worsen.
- Treatment planned:
  - Rest and fluids.
  - Acetaminophen (paracetamol) as needed for comfort/fever.
  - Monitor for fever or worsening symptoms; re-evaluate in 2–3 days if not improving.
  - If feverish or cough persists/breathing worsens, consider antibiotics for chest infection at follow-up.
- Relevant referrals: None.

2. Chronic disease management (type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension)
- Assessment: Diabetes and hypertension appear under regular care; on Metformin and lisinopril; currently controlled based on interview (no labs or vitals provided).
- Differential diagnoses: Not applicable.
- Investigations planned: None documented.
- Treatment planned:
  - Continue current medications (Metformin; lisinopril).
  - Counseling on reducing alcohol intake due to blood pressure and diabetes considerations.
- Relevant referrals: None.

3. Health maintenance and activity/work considerations
- Assessment: Not formalized as a separate issue, but advised work modifications during acute illness.
- Plan:
  - If possible, take 1–2 days off work to rest and reduce infectious risk; return to work early next week if improving.
  - If cough or breathing worsens, or if symptoms persist beyond a short period, return for re-evaluation.

Quality checks (document_quality):

- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (BP, pulse, respiratory rate, temperature) not documented.
  - No explicit physical examination findings recorded beyond brief subjective ENT and respiratory reports.
  - No laboratory tests or imaging results ordered or reported.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Conversation was generally clear; no major noise or inaudible portions affecting key clinical information.
